questions.question: The projected income statement and the cash budget respectively ask:
options: Will the business be profitable, and will there be money in the bank
Will there be money in the bank, and will the business be profitable
What was earned last year, and what will be earned next year
What does SARS require, and what does the bank require

questions.question: Depreciation appears in:
options: The projected income statement only — no rand ever leaves the bank for wear

questions.question: A new delivery scooter bought for cash appears in:
options: The projected income statement in full
The cash budget in full in the month of payment; only its depreciation reaches the income statement

questions.question: A loan received from the bank is:
options: Income in the projected income statement
A receipt in the cash budget only — borrowing is not income

questions.question: Credit sales: July R60 000, August R90 000, September R110 000; collections 25 percent same month, 55 percent next, 15 percent second month. September's collections are:
The 5 percent of credit sales that never appears in the schedule represents:
options: Bad debts — the absence in the cash budget matching the expense in the income statement

questions.question: Only 25 percent of credit sales paying in the month of sale means:
options: The business collects most cash immediately
The business finances seventy-five percent of every month's credit sales for at least a month

questions.question: August purchases of R70 000 paid in September with a 4 percent settlement discount require a payment of:
options: R67 200 — and starting to miss such discounts signals cash trouble

subtopics.title: Building and Reading the Cash Budget

questions.question: Dube Cycles' September: receipts R155 000, payments R147 000, opening overdraft R3 000. The closing balance is:
options: R5 000 favourable — a surplus of R8 000 absorbing the overdraft

questions.question: The three chained lines at the foot of every cash budget column are:
options: Sales, cost of sales, gross profit
Surplus or shortfall, opening balance, closing balance — linking each month to the next

questions.question: A projected shortfall month is best understood as:
options: A reason to abandon the budget
Information arriving early enough to act — arrange facilities, delay discretionary payments, chase collections

questions.question: Because more than half of September's cash arrives through the collection schedule, a single bad sales month will:
options: Echo through two more months of collections — so the budget must be re-run when projections move

subtopics.title: Budget Against Actual, and the Ethics of Forecasting

questions.question: Advertising underspent by R4 500 while sales fell R24 000 short is best described as:
options: A false economy — saving four and a half thousand to lose twenty-four
A favourable variance with no further meaning

questions.question: Salaries and wages overspent by R6 000 should be judged:
options: Only after the explanation — overtime for the stock count, a negotiated increase, or uncontrolled casual hiring are different stories
By ignoring it if under ten percent

questions.question: Padding a budget means:
options: Adding a contingency line approved by the board
Overstating expense budgets in advance so that underspending later looks like discipline
Preparing the budget after the period

questions.question: A fantasy sales forecast shown to a bank corrupts the loan decision because:
options: The bank will demand higher interest
Every downstream figure — collections, purchases, cash — inherits the fiction, so money is lent into a lie

subtopics.title: The Month Written Down Before It Happens

questions.question: Karabo keeps two lists because:
options: Profitable and broke are different things — bills arrive on dates, not averages

questions.question: The wear on her camera bodies belongs on:
options: The profit list only — nobody collects cash for wear

questions.question: The R2 500 her sister repays her is:
options: An expense when lent, income when returned
Money in on the cash list, but not income — her own money coming home

questions.question: The client who might never settle the invoice appears as:
options: A receipt in the cash budget
A bad-debts line on the profit list, and on the cash list simply money that fails to appear

subtopics.title: When Will the Money Actually Arrive?

questions.question: Invoices of July R6 000, August R8 000 and September R10 000, on the 25-55-15 rhythm, deliver September collections of:
September's bank balance being mostly August's work means:
options: Karabo is her clients' unpaid banker for a month or more on most of each invoice

questions.question: Budgeting the 5 percent that never arrives as loss from the start is:
options: The honest way to plan — the failure is expected, not a surprise

questions.question: Paying the print lab R4 800 instead of R5 000 shows that:
options: She short-paid and owes the difference
The 4 percent settlement discount was earned by punctuality — and the first missed discount is a warning light about her own cash

questions.question: Bookings down R3 200 beside marketing underspent by R600 tells the story that:
options: The saving was the most expensive purchase of the month

questions.question: The overspent travel line is judged fairly by:
options: Reading it beside the extra out-of-town weddings it carried — variances are judged in pairs and stories

questions.question: A company freezing training while directors' travel grows has:
options: Published its true priorities in numbers — variances reveal values

questions.question: The budgeting cycle, in order, is:
options: Write the month before it happens, live it, compare the columns, explain the gaps, correct, and carry the lesson forward
